steps.content: You force your way into the control room. Behind you, voices shout, and people try to stop you. Without looking back, you slap the door controls and lock them all outside. Then you face Isomer directly.

steps.speaker: Flawed Schorl
steps.content: Chief, calm down. The current situation is...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: "Security" concerns?! Quit joking!

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The Mania frequency spectrum from that chaos cube matches that of the Underground's. If there really is a mole within the Observation Hub, then the prime suspect is Isomer.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You received my report. Yet instead of investigating the real suspect, you replaced the entire core team?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Where is <size=45><color=#fb9259>Lemma</color>?! Is she alone?! Did you lock her up?!</size>
Schorl tries to explain, but the person being questioned speaks first.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: I knew it. You were the one who submitted that evidence against me. You had Summer keep tabs on me, testing me. I must admit, she did well.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: Just by staying close to me, she managed to gather that much information. That girl is indeed a genius. Who knows how she pulled it off.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: And you're good at putting geniuses to work, Chief. I thought I was careful enough around you, yet you still managed to blindside me. What a pain in the neck.
Cold, morose, and arrogant. The sight of her makes you sick.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: If those documents had been worth anything, you never would've walked away unscathed!

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Do you have Undergrounders inside EDGE pulling strings for you too? Or does humanity's highest council actually favor ruthless opportunists like you?
She sits in silence, studying your fury. For a long moment, she simply watches. Then, slowly, very slowly, she smiles.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: ...Look at you. Right now, you remind me of Lambert, Laplace, and so many others. Every one of those brilliant minds wore that same frustrated look when I defeated them. It's almost pitiful.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: This anger will get you nothing. And all this just for some kids? Chief, even at this juncture, you're still looking out for others... It only makes you look more foolish.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Isomer!!
The unrestrained rage is futile yet delicious. It tears open just enough breathing room in this suffocating space. The angrier ${PlayerName} becomes, the stronger Isomer's twisted pleasure grows.
Let's give him a treat.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: I didn't do anything. Those geniuses were discarded by those who <color=#fb9259>used</color> them.
She stares at her accuser, a cruel smile curling at the corner of her mouth.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: To conquer the unknown for humanity, they were fashioned into perfect tools. They possess neither common sense nor conventional ways of thinking. They see nothing but truth and knowledge. They're so brilliant, and arrogant. And naturally, they fail to see what their patrons truly wanted from them.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: Nirvana kept BR-003 for the Hypercubes. The council and the city backed her because they wanted stronger catastrophe weapons. All the resources, funding, time, and political capital poured into that project... and look what she did with it in the end.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: Dimension? What even is that? What about practical applications? The return on investment? Heh. And she still had the nerve to act all superior... Once they're out of the lab, these so-called <color=#fb9259>geniuses</color> are no better than fools. She was finally about to give in... and then you went and gave her another push.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: Oh, Chief... You're too good at giving pep talks.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Stop twisting the facts! As a scientist, she dedicated herself to her research. As an EDGE representative, she always chose the path that would serve humanity's fight against Mania.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Lemma never once failed to perform her duty. Those corrupt bastards conspired against her. They didn't even bother coming up with some "rational" or "scientific" justification. They simply tore her down with their dirty tricks. This isn't over yet. But that's not why I came here.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: Heh. Then why are you here? To congratulate me?

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: You never thought I deserved this position. You think cunning, ambitious strategists are inferior to those brilliant, idealistic geniuses.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Stop putting words in my mouth. I never said that, and neither did Lemma!
You step forward and slam both hands on the desk, leaning in to glare at Isomer.

steps.speaker: Option
options: She's always seen you as a genius!

steps.speaker: Lemma
steps.content: I'm extremely selective when it comes to my team. I've read every single paper she's published. From her days in academia, to her work on the Black Ring project, to the years she spent leading her own research team as a professor... That woman was once a remarkable <color=#fb9259>scholar</color>.

steps.speaker: Lemma
steps.content: She's well-rounded, objective, rigorous, and imaginative. She had a particular talent for synthesizing theories, integrating dissimilar ideas, and identifying new avenues for breakthroughs. Her experimental work was impeccable as well. Isomer's accomplishments are truly outstanding. Otherwise, 02 would never have handpicked her.

steps.speaker: Lemma
steps.content: ...I was impressed by those papers. The author was clearly intelligent, passionate, and committed to her work. That's the most valuable type of researcher. If only that old fool Lambert hadn't held her back for so many years...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You were an exception in the Black Ring project. The elite there looked down on your ordinary background. They exploited your talent, but they also feared it. They used every trick to undermine you. You never had a chance to rise.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Finally, in N.F. 104, Nirvana took the Super-Loop Communication system you'd improved to create the Inner Bay mining disaster. Then, a Black Ring erupted unexpectedly, and once again, you became the scapegoat.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: After that, you were placed on leave and underwent treatment, removed from all frontline work. For nine years, you produced nothing. Tell me, Isomer... how much of that was because they pushed you aside? And how much was because you couldn't bear knowing the technology you had created to make the world safer had been used to kill?

steps.speaker: Lemma
steps.content: What was she thinking? If she realized she'd gone down the wrong path, she could have changed course. If people were misusing her research, she should have fought them for it. Didn't she become the Director? Which means she has more power than ever. She could've done so much more, gone so much further.

steps.speaker: Lemma
steps.content: But is that position cursed or something? Does it corrupt everyone who takes it? Her research has stagnated, and all she cares about now is petty politics. She even had the nerve to tell me that it's because "she's not as talented as we are." What a ridiculous excuse!

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: To Lemma, talent is never a competition. She's never felt inferior to Summer, nor has she ever looked down on you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: She sees all of you as scholars making contributions to humanity. She believes all talent should be directed where it's most needed.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: She's always hoped you could come back to your role as a researcher, back to that path reserved for a true scientist!
Isomer closes her eyes, but the memories still stir.

steps.speaker: Lemma
steps.content: I don't care how you treat me. That's irrelevant to science, to humanity. But take a good look at yourself. What have you become? You're even more pathetic than that idiot Summer!

steps.speaker: Lemma
steps.content: A genius's mind should be devoted to the pursuit of truth and knowledge. It's a gift to all humanity! And look what you've wasted yours on?!
...It's still so suffocating.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: Me? A fellow genius? No... The gap between people like us and true geniuses is far greater than you can imagine.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: ...But none of that matters anymore.
Isomer looks up. Schorl is here. No matter how their form or attitude changes, these devices serve only EDGE—only a "certain representative." She knows this.
But here, now, none of that matters anymore. Isomer speaks.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: Regarding the replacement of EDGE-07, security risks and cooperation issues were certainly factors. But they accounted for less than thirty percent of the decision.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: The real reason is the self-reformation of the <color=#fb9259>genius</color> system.
She looks at you. The turbulent emotions from before seem to have faded completely, her voice tepid as still water.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: Objectively speaking, <color=#fb9259>geniuses</color> are merely superior specimens within humanity. They are efficient decision-making units society requires. The exceptions our civilization relies on to solve all unknowns. But their traits aren't dominant enough. They're rare, and the screening and nurturing of these individuals are extremely difficult.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: Traditional society glorified science and encouraged generations of people to enter the funnel. The education system then sifted them through layer after layer of selection, directing resources toward those deemed most promising. And after all that? It produced only a handful of "geniuses." The results were inconsistent, resources were misallocated, and the overall efficiency was abysmal.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: And now, that system has decayed even further. Academia no longer cultivates talent. It's become breeding grounds for corruption. Society no longer values knowledge. Money and fame are what people are after now.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: Look at the world outside. The disasters keep escalating, city-states grow more competitive with each other, and civilization's demand for "geniuses" only climbs higher. EDGE is desperately looking for a more efficient way to secure that resource. And that's when the <color=#fb9259>most brilliant scientist</color> stepped in...

steps.speaker: Abhorrent Memory
steps.content: Genius worship is nothing more than a romanticized notion born of scarcity. Much like the way financial markets chase high-performance chips. Though I suppose such mystification could be a rational adaptation for a society still in its earlier stages of development...

steps.speaker: Abhorrent Memory
steps.content: But we do need to tackle the scarcity issue. Hmm... We can't optimize every stage of the pipeline just yet, but perhaps we can expand the base pool through other means, and create a more refined environment, where we can improve the efficiency of the screening and cultivation cycle.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: That genius found a way to manufacture geniuses. She studied Mania's effects on consciousness and leveraged the authority of her position. She was able to screen for high-intelligence individuals who met her criteria on a far larger scale, and through far more rational and stable means.

Heterogeneous Trial 0.1: Initial screening of all newborns based on adaptability and basic traits. Scope: Centered around Banyan Medical College Hospital, covering Eastside, West District, and DisCity's satellite towns. 0.1.4: Sampling groups expanded to include ages 4, 8, and 12. Preliminary assessment: Newborn screening still yields the highest pass rate across all sampling groups. 0.2.1: Current test metrics focus on intelligence, environmental adaptability, physical capacity, and Mania tolerance. Additional metric added: behavioral compliance assessment. 0.3.4: Exceptional candidates approved through final review will be permitted direct entry to Paradeisos. Special files will be created for unselected final review candidates to facilitate long-term monitoring and follow-up. If they pass subsequent tests, they may still be chosen for the cultivation program.
[Insert: Memory of children idolizing their heroes][Small idol CG]

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: The critical window is puberty, when the specimens are highly malleable, passionate, impulsive, and impressionable. More importantly, the new model allows for effective control of the cultivation cycle. The costs of screening, maintenance, and replacement can all be greatly reduced.

steps.speaker: Abhorrent Memory
steps.content: We're currently in a transitional phase, so some degree of socialization needs to be preserved in them. I suggest assigning "families" to the earlier batches. My thanks in advance to all departments for their cooperation.

steps.speaker: Abhorrent Memory
steps.content: That Sinner named Summer has greatly inspired me as well. Heh... Shall we pursue a new experiment in the future?

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: Yes, if this batch fails to meet our expectations, it can simply be replaced. It'll also be a good opportunity to reassess the handover process. There's no need to trouble ourselves over it.

steps.speaker: Abhorrent Memory
steps.content: This is a tremendous scientific breakthrough. Once the process is proven viable, talent will no longer be in shortage. It will become a stable, replaceable, high-quality resource that can be rationally allocated. Humanity should celebrate this achievement.
In the pitch-black room, darkness is strangling every throat, mocking the anger of those who still dare to hope.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: They were never seen as treasures to begin with, Chief.

You stand speechless, frozen to the core. That girl who takes such pride in her gift. The scholar who swore to live up to the "genius" title. That child who works so hard to catch up to those who came before her... Somewhere beyond your sight, at this very moment, someone has just given her a careless push...
...Shattering her completely. A star shining so brightly, yet made of something so deeply fragile.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...Lemma. She doesn't know yet, does she?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: After you've learned about all this... how do you feel about those children now?
<i>How does she feel?
The question catches Isomer off guard.

steps.speaker: Abhorrent Memory
steps.content: So, how do you feel now, Isomer? The word "talent" has always made you feel inferior and inadequate.

steps.speaker: EDGE-02 & Isomer
steps.content:
Are you finally relieved?
...I feel relieved.
At last, she lets out a long-held breath.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: I'll answer one more question for you, Chief. You and I do share a special connection.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: The BR-002 eruption in N.F. 104 dealt me a devastating blow. I was demoted and expelled from frontline work. For a long time afterward, I couldn't face my research again. My thoughts were clouded by regret and anxiety.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: So, nine years later, when the remaining half of the Corpus returned to Drifter Camp, and the Black Ring's shadow loomed once more... it felt like fate. My mind cleared up again. Yet my first thought was no longer how to fight the disaster or save lives. I worked tirelessly designing the defense zone, but it was not out of any noble ideal.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: The moment the secondary eruption of the West District Black Ring happened... I felt no grief, only relief... joy, even. I thought, now they'd all see how wrong Lambert had been. I could climb higher over his dead body. I...

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: Would become the next <color=#fb9259>Director</color>...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You...
You need to say something. But what? Your mind has gone blank.
She catches the struggle written across your face. She smiles faintly and spares you the trouble.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: So, you shouldn't feel torn, Chief. You don't need to trust me. Even if I weren't serving the Sillage Society, you and I could never walk the same path again.
Isomer rises to her feet.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: The report you filed against me wasn't ignored. EDGE reviewed it carefully. They investigated me thoroughly, fairly, and without bias.
The control room door opens. She puts on her coat and walks out.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: I'm not the spy who sabotaged the Hub. I would never have left behind such obvious traces that could destroy my career.
All the dark, chaotic emotions are sealed away once more, locked into that cold, rigid cube in her hand.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: But I do have one more piece of information for you. <color=#fb9259>The Sillage Society</color> that you're investigating... might be closer than you think.
She stops before you and offers one last quiet remark.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: Think about it. Someone who has climbed to the top as I have, who holds that much information, who has the means to help you come after me... Do you really think a person like that can keep their hands clean?
[Celine's portrait flashes on screen]
You snap back to awareness and reach out to stop her.
The moment passes. The people waiting outside flood into the room, and any chance for further conversation vanishes.
At the same time, your comms device vibrates. Another shocking post has just appeared on that academic exposé forum you've been monitoring. A single glance at the headline leaves you stunned.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: This is...?!

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: Heh... You'd better hurry back. Don't let outsiders get hold of the evidence first and drag you down with it. Find out who the mole is, the one who let the Underground into the Black Ring. I'll continue helping you best I can.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: After all, this is my Hub now. And going forward, I'll need it to secure my place in EDGE, to "<color=#fb9259>fight for humanity</color>."
[Scene Change]

The door of the dark chamber is suddenly smashed open. The sheriff bursts in and shouts with his gun raised.

steps.speaker: Sheriff
steps.content: Hands up! Ugh! Cough, cough! ...What kind of hellhole is this?

The room is barely thirty square meters in size, yet it is crammed with computers stacked three meters high, forming a crooked, makeshift wall. None are powered on. Pitch-black screens stare like hollow eyes at the intruder. The whole mass resembles some grotesque creature, reeking of old plastic and corroded metal.
The sheriff waves away the dust swirling before him and tiptoes toward one of the strange computers. A few quick keystrokes, and a lengthy list instantly pops up on the screen.

Countless commissions for ghostwritten papers, forged experimental data, and leaked exam questions, spanning every academic discipline. Worse still, the client list runs for several pages, each name paired with matching transaction records. A clear, damning ledger of academic fraud involving dozens, if not hundreds, of elite students.

This is precisely the "criminal evidence" he came for. After confirming several untouchable surnames are indeed on the list, the sheriff deletes them with trembling hands. His real mission finally complete, he breathes a sigh of relief.

steps.speaker: Sheriff
steps.content: ...To think that even United University has been tainted by vermin like this. Yeah, these lowlifes never should have been given any opportunities. A stain on academia will sooner or later become a threat to society...

steps.speaker: Sheriff
steps.content: Who's there?! You...!
He whips the gun around. In the shadows, there is nothing but the stack of decrepit, second-hand monitors. No one...?
No, something's wrong! The sheriff shudders. He clearly sees one of those square "monitors" begin to tremble. It's... giggling.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: Hehe, you caught me... hehehehe...

steps.speaker: Sheriff
steps.content: Tsk... What a freak... Knew it was some crazy kid.

steps.speaker: Sheriff
steps.content: Hands up! You're charged with spreading rumors, defamation, inciting public panic, and undermining the sacred education system of DisCity! You're under arrest! Do not resist!
The computer head laughs even harder.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: Me? Crazy? Rumors? Defamation? And... undermining the sacred... education system of DisCity? ...Are you sure?
Her screen flickers violently, grotesque "facial" expressions flashing across it quickly. Pixel's body begins writhing as she shrieks with laughter.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: Who's the crazy one here? The people faking research? The ones profiting from predatory student loans? The scammers exploiting science for money? And what about those who wrap themselves in academic authority while inventing new ways to kill and bury the truth? Aren't they crazier than I am?

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: No one is really that crazy! They're all PERFECTLY NORMAL!!! And a humble ghostwriter like me is just doing my part for DisCity's sacred education system!

Her laughter erupts into a piercing screech. The sheriff's body jerks, and he fires. Several bullets strike Pixel. One shatters the upper-right corner of the monitor screen, and it goes black. Her laugh stops, and her dance freezes. Her entire body becomes as still as a statue.
Then, the statue melts rapidly, forming a shapeless, glue-like puddle on the floor. This isn't a human. It's just a... a 3D-printed monster? A Sinner!

But there's no time to report it. From outside, through the door gap, the poor sheriff hears some rustling noise. Numerous shadows slip into the room. Drawn by the commotion, they've stumbled upon a decent snack.

steps.speaker: Sheriff
steps.content: What the...! What did you do?! You... Don't come any closer... No... AHHH!!!

What follows is like a scene taken out of a clichéd splatter horror film. One after another, the monitors are smashed to pieces, and new screens flicker to life in their place. Finally, Pixel's face fills the entire room. Her fluorescent gaze bathes everything in cold light.

Every computer head in the room erupts in laughter, applauding the madness, celebrating the filth. Betray and be betrayed! This magnificent spectacle deserves nothing less than the highest performance art award!

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: Hahahaha! Let the false brilliance explode! Let the rotten reason collapse! Meet your fall, all of you!!!

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: The sacred halls of academia? The pale blue firmament? It's all so filthy! Every last one of you is rotten to the core!
